c: Ali bin Sahl told us: Hajjaj told us: Abu Jaafar Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah Al-Riyahi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah or someone else.
m: Abu Jaafar was unsure. He said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the lote tree. He said: The light of the Creator covered it, and the angels covered it like crows when they land on trees. Then he said: Ask him.

x: God Almighty says: His sight did not deviate to the right or to the left from what he saw, meaning, nor did it exceed what he was commanded to do, meaning: It rose above the limit that was set for it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
His sight did not swerve
, nor did it go beyond what it was commanded to do. He said, It did not swerve to the right or to the left, nor did it go beyond what it was commanded to do. Our grandfather Ibn Hamid said:

c: Mihran told us on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi,
m: h
His sight did not swerve

nor did it go astray. He said that he saw Gabriel in the form of an angel. He said: Thabit Mahran, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
His sight did not swerve
nor did it go beyond the bounds. He said: It did not swerve: it went right or left, nor did it go beyond the bounds.

x: And his saying,
h
He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord
, God Almighty says: Muhammad saw there some of the greatest signs and evidence of his Lord.
The interpreters differed regarding these great verses.
Some of them said: He saw a green leaf that covered the horizon.
Who said that?

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
He has certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord
. He said: A green leaf from Paradise that filled the horizon.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: Abdullah said, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud:
m: Among the greatest signs of his Lord he said: A green leaf that filled the horizon.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-A’mash, that Ibn Mas’ud said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a green blanket from Paradise that filled the horizon.

x: Others said: He saw Gabriel in his true form.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd, regarding his statement,
h
He has certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord
, said: Gabriel saw him in his creation in the heavens, the distance between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: God the Most High says: Have you considered, O polytheists, Al-Lat? It is from God, and the letter taa was added to it, making it feminine, just as it is said ‘Amr for the male and ‘Umra for the female, and just as it is said for the male ‘Abbas, then it is said for the female ‘Abbasa. Thus the polytheists named their idols with the names of God the Most High and His names are sanctified. They said: From God is Al-Lat, and from the Almighty is Al-‘Uzza. They claimed that they are the daughters of God. God is exalted above what they say and fabricate. So God the Most High said to them: Have you considered, O you who claim that Al-Lat, Al-‘Uzza, and Manat, the third, are the daughters of God? Do you have the male? He says: Do you choose for yourselves a male from among your children and dislike a female for her and assign for Him a female whom you would not like for yourselves, but you kill her out of your dislike for them.

The reciters differed regarding his saying: Al-Lat. The majority of the reciters of the regions recited it with a light ta’, according to the meaning that I described. It was mentioned that Al-Lat was a house in Nakhalah that was worshipped by the Quraysh.
Some of them said: It was in Taif.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? As for Al-Lat, it was in Taif.

c: Yunus told me: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? He said: Al-Lat was a house in a palm tree that the Quraysh worshipped. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Abu Saleh read it as Al-Lat with a shaddah on the ta and made it an attribute of the idol that they worshipped. They said: He was a man who mixed gruel for the pilgrims, and when he died, they devoted themselves to his grave and worshipped it. The report was mentioned by the one who said it:

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza? He said: He used to mix gruel for the pilgrims, so he devoted himself to his grave. He said: Muammil told us, he said:

c: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: Have you seen Al-Lat? He said: Al-Lat used to knead gruel for the pilgrims.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, Al-Lat said:
m: He used to mix gruel, then he died, so they devoted themselves to his grave.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, Al-Lat, he said: A man used to mix gruel for the polytheists, then he died, so they devoted themselves to his grave.

c: Ahmad bin Hisham told us: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: regarding his statement, Al-Lat, he said: Al-Lat was the one who was in charge of their gods, mixing gruel for them, and he was in Taif.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me: Abu Ubaid told us: Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Abu al-Ashhab, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: He used to mix gruel for the pilgrims. The first of the two readings that is more correct in our view is the reading of the one who read with a light ta’, based on the meaning that was described to the reader, as well, due to the consensus of the proof from the readers of the regions.

x: Some of them said: They were trees that they worshipped.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And al-Uzza. He said: al-Uzza is a tree.

x: Others said: Al-Uzza was a white stone.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: Al-Uzza is a white stone.

x: Others said: It was a house in Taif that was worshipped by Thaqif.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, And Al-Uzza, that Al-Uzza was a house in Taif that the Thaqif worshipped.

x: Others said it was in Batn Nakhal.
Who said that?

evidence.text: The reciters differed regarding his saying: Al-Lat.
The majority of the reciters of the regions recited it with a light ta’, according to the meaning that I described.
Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Abu Saleh read it as Al-Lat with a shaddah on the ta and made it an attribute of the idol that they worshipped.

The first of the two readings that is more correct in our view is the reading of the one who read with a light ta’, based on the meaning that was described to the reader, as well, due to the consensus of the proof from the readers of the regions.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: And Manat is the third other. He said: As for Manat, it was the dried-up gods that they used to worship, meaning Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement, And Manat, the third, the other, he said: Manat was a house in Al-Mushallal that the Banu Ka’b worshipped. The Arabists differed on the reason for stopping at Al-Lat and Manat.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: If you are silent, you say Al-Lat. Likewise, Manat, you say: Manat. He said: Some of them said: Al-Lat, so he made it from Al-Lat, so he made it from Al-Lat which is yalta, and the language of the Arabs is that they stop at what has the Haa with the Taa, they say: I saw Talhat, and everything that is written, they stop at it with the Taa, like the blessing of your Lord and the tree.
Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to stop at Al-Lat with the Haa, Have you seen Al-Lat?

Others of them used to say: The choice in everything that is not added is to be with the Haa, mercy from my Lord and a tree that comes out, and what is added is permissible with the Haa and the Taa, so the Taa is for the addition and the Haa because it is singular and stopped at, unlike the second. This third statement is the most widespread of the languages and most of them among the Arabs, even though the other has a known aspect.

Some of the people of knowledge of the speech of the Arabs from the people of Basra used to say: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat are the third, idols of stone that were inside the Kaaba and they worshipped them.

And his saying, Do you have the male and He has the female? He says: Do you claim that you have the male that you are satisfied with and God has the female that you are not satisfied with for yourselves?
h
That is indeed an unfair division

. God Almighty says: This division of yours is an unfair, unequal, deficient, and incomplete division, because you have attributed to your Lord children that which you dislike for yourselves, and you have preferred for yourselves what pleases you. The Arabs say, Darruh haqquhu with a kasra on the ḍād, and ḍazzuh with a ḍamma on the ḍād, so I deprive him and I deprive him, and that is if I deprive him of his right and prevent him from it.

c: I was told on the authority of Muammar ibn al-Muthanna,
m: who said, Al-Akhfash recited to me: If you turn away from us, we will disparage you, and if you are absent, your arrow will be pierced and your nose will be swollen. Some Arabs say dhizi with a fatha on the dad and without the hamza, and some say dhaazi with a fatha and hamza, and dhuzai with a damma and hamza. No one recited any of these languages. As for dhizi with a kasra, it is fa’la with a damma on the fa’. The dad was broken in it as it was broken in their saying qawm bayd and ‘ayn, which is a verb because its singular is bayda’ and ‘ayna’, to combine the plural, the two, and the one. Likewise, they disliked the damma of dhizi, so you say dawza for fear that it would become with a waw, which is from the ya’. Al-Farra’ said: I decided on the damma of the first letter because the feminine adjectives come either with a fatha or a damma, so the fatha is sakra sakra and ’asha thirsty, and the damma is the female and the pregnant. So if it is a noun and not an adjective, its first letter is broken, like his saying, And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers (al-Dhariyat 51:55). Its first letter is broken because it is a noun and not an adjective. Likewise, al-Shi’ra poetry has a kasra at the beginning because it is a noun and not an adjective. In a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of his statement, an unfair division, he said: The people of interpretation, although their wording differed in expressing it, some of them said: a crooked division.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: That is indeed a division that is unfair, he said: Crooked.

x: Others said it was an unfair division.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us that
m: Saeed was killed, on the authority of Qatada: That is an unfair division. He said: An unjust division.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: An unfair division means an unjust division.

c: Muhammad bin Hafs Abu Ubaid Al-Wasa’i told us: Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Umrah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, That would be an unfair division, he said: That would be a permissible division in which there is no right.

x: Others said: It is an incomplete division.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan:
m: That is an unfair division. He said: It is incomplete.

x: Others said: A contrary division.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd, regarding his statement,
h
That is indeed an unfair division

, said: They attributed daughters to God, the Blessed and Exalted, and they attributed daughters to the angels of God and worshipped them. He recited, Or has He taken from what He creates daughters and preferred you with sons? And when He gives you good tidings? Az-Zukhruf 43:16-17. He recited, And they attribute daughters to God An-Nahl 16:57 to the end of the verse. He said: They ascribe to God a son as the Jews and Christians did. He recited, Thus said those before them Al-Baqarah 2:118. He said: In the speech of the Arabs, the unfair division means: opposition. He recited, They are only names which you have named, you and your fathers.

x: God Almighty says: These names that you have named, namely Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other, are nothing but names that you and your fathers, O polytheists, have named, and your fathers before you. God has not sent them down meaning by these names He says: God has not permitted that to you nor has He given you permission to do it.

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement, of authority...to the end of the verse. And His statement,
h
They follow nothing but conjecture

, God Almighty says: These polytheists follow nothing in these names by which they named their gods except conjecture that what they say is true, not certainty. And what their souls desire, He says: And their own desires, because they did not take that from a revelation that came to them from God, nor from a Messenger of God who informed them of it. Rather, it is a breach from their own selves, or they took it from their fathers who were disbelieving in God just as they are. And His statement,
h
And indeed there has come to them from their Lord guidance

, means: And indeed these polytheists have come from their Lord to clarify what they are uncertain about, and that is their naming of al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat the third with these names and their worship of them. He says: Indeed there has come to them from their Lord guidance in that and clarification by the revelation that We revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they should not be worshipped and that worship is only appropriate for God, the One, the Compeller. Ibn Zayd said about this:

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And there has certainly come to them guidance from their Lord
, but they did not benefit from it.

x: God Almighty says: Or did Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, desire what God gave him of this honor with which He honored him of prophethood and messengership and sent down revelation to him and wished for that, so his Lord gave it to him? To God belongs whatever is in the Hereafter and in this world. He gives to whomever He wills of His creation whatever He wills and withholds from whomever He wills of them whatever He wills. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement,
h
Or does man have what he desires
? He said, And if Muhammad desired this, then that is his right.

x: God Almighty says: To God belongs the Hereafter and the first.
And His statement,
h
And how many are there angels in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all
? God Almighty says:
h
And how many are there angels in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all

with God for those for whom they intercede, unless they intercede for him after God has given them permission to intercede for whomever He wills among them to intercede for and is pleased with. He says: And after He is pleased with His angels who intercede for him to intercede for him, so that their intercession will then benefit him. This is only a rebuke from God Almighty to His idol worshippers and the leaders of Quraysh and others who used to say, We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to God. (al-Zumar 39:3). So God Almighty said to them: The intercession of My angels who are with Me will not benefit those for whom they intercede except after My permission for them to intercede for him and My pleasure, so how about the intercession of those besides them?

c: So He informed them that
m: the intercession of those they worship besides Him will not benefit them.

x: God Almighty says: Those who do not believe in the resurrection in the Hereafter, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, call the angels of God by female names. This is because they used to say: They are the daughters of God. And in a similar manner to what we said about his statement, Naming the female, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Sumayyah the female, he said: females.

x: And His statement:
h
And they have no knowledge of it God Almighty says

: And they have no knowledge of what they say about calling the angels female names. They follow nothing but conjecture. He says: They follow nothing in that except conjecture, meaning that they say that based on conjecture without knowledge. His saying,
h
And suspicion does not replace the truth at all
, means that suspicion does not replace the truth at all, so it can take its place.
And His saying,
h
So turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance

, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So leave, O Muhammad, whoever turns away from the remembrance of God and does not believe in Him and declare His Oneness. His saying,
h
And he only wanted the life of this world
, means that he did not seek what is with God in the Hereafter, but rather he sought the adornments of this worldly life and sought to remain in it.

God Almighty says: What these people who do not believe in the Hereafter say about the angels, by calling them female names, their level of knowledge means they have no knowledge other than this disbelief in God and associating partners with Him based on conjecture without certain knowledge.
Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, “
h
So turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance and desires only the life of this world

. That is the extent of their knowledge.” He said: He says that they have no knowledge except that which they are in of disbelief in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their plotting against what came from God. He said: And these are the people of polytheism. And His statement: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided. God Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is most knowing of who has deviated from His way in His previous knowledge and does not believe, and that way is Islam. And He is most knowing of who is guided. He says: And your Lord is most knowing of who has found his way and followed it in His previous knowledge, and that way is also Islam.

x: God Almighty says: “And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He sends astray whom He wills, and He is most knowing of them. “That He may reward those who do evil for what they have done.” That is, to reward those of His creation who disobeyed Him and did evil by disobeying Him, and He will reward them with the Fire for it. And He may reward those who do good with good. That is, to reward those who obeyed Him and did good by obeying Him in this world with good, which is Paradise, and He will reward them with it. It was said: He meant by that the people of polytheism and faith.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Abdullah bin Ayyash told me: Zaid bin Aslam said
m: about the statement of God, That He may reward those who do evil for what they have done and reward those who do good Al-Mu’minun.

x: And His statement,
h
Those who avoid the major sins

, means: Those who stay away from the major sins that God has forbidden and prohibited for them, so they do not approach them. This is associating partners with God, and what we have explained in His statement,
h
If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden
, We will remove from you your lesser sins.
r
(An-Nisa’: 31)
. His saying: And indecencies are adultery and the like, for which God has imposed a punishment. And his saying:
h
Except for a few
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of except in this place.

Some of them said: It means a discontinuous exception. They said: The meaning of the statement is: Those who avoid major sins and indecencies except for the few sins and indecencies that they committed in the pre-Islamic era, for God has forgiven them for it and will not hold them accountable for it.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities
, except minor ones, meaning: except what has already happened.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities

, except for the minor ones, he said: The polytheists were only working with us yesterday, so God, the Almighty, revealed, except for the minor ones, which refers to what they did in the pre-Islamic era. He said: The minor ones are the major sins and immoralities that they committed in the pre-Islamic era before Islam, and He forgave them for them when they converted to Islam.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, who said:
m: A man asked Zayd ibn Thabit about this verse: Those who avoid major sins and immoralities, except minor ones, so he said: God has forbidden you immoralities, both apparent and secret.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Abdullah bin Ayyash told me: Zaid bin Aslam said
m: about the statement of God,
h
Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities

, except minor sins, he said: The major sins of polytheism and immoralities, such as adultery, were abandoned when they entered Islam, so God forgave them for what they had committed and committed of that before Islam.

x: Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language directed the interpretation of except in this place to this aspect that I mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said in his interpretation of that: They were not given permission to touch something that is not from the indecencies nor from the major sins. And something may be excepted from something that is not from it on the basis of a pronoun that has been refrained from, so it is a metaphor: except that he touches something that is not from the indecencies nor from the major sins.

A town that has no companions except the camels and the wild donkeys Al-Ya'afir: the gazelles and Al-Ays: the camels, and they are not people, so it is as if he said: It has no companions except that it has gazelles and camels.
Some of them said: Al-Ya'afir is the red gazelle and Al-Ays is the white one.
A group of interpreters said something similar to this.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, that Ibn Mas’ud said:
m: The fornication of the eyes is looking, the fornication of the lips is kissing, the fornication of the hands is touching, and the fornication of the feet is walking. The private parts confirm or deny that. If he comes forward with his private parts, then he is a fornicator, otherwise it is a lick.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, who said: Ibn Tawus told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: Those who avoid major sins and immoralities, only minor ones. Indeed, your Lord is Vast in forgiveness. He is most knowing of you when He created you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim yourselves to be pure. He is most knowing of who fears Him. who said: I have never seen anything more resembling a lick than what Abu Hurayrah said on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God has decreed for the son of Adam his share of fornication, and it will inevitably overtake him. The fornication of the eyes is looking, and the fornication of the tongue is speech. The soul desires and longs, and the private parts confirm or deny that.”
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Except for a small amount
, he said: If it comes beforehand, it is adultery, and if it comes afterward, it is a small amount.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Mansour bin Abd al-Rahman told us:
m: I asked al-Sha’bi about the statement of God, They avoid major sins and immoralities, except minor sins. He said: It is less than adultery. Then he mentioned to us on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: Adultery of the eyes is what you look at, adultery of the hand is what you touch, adultery of the foot is what you walk, and intercourse with the private parts.

c: Muhammad ibn Muammar told me: Yaʿqub told us: Wahib told us: Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khathim ibn Amr al-Qari told us:
m: Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafiʿ, who is called Ibn Lubabah at-Taʿifi, told us: I asked Abu Hurayrah about the statement of God,
h
Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities
, except minor sins. He said: Kissing, winking, looking, and intimate contact. If circumcision touches circumcision, then ritual ablution is required, which is adultery.
b.via: Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khathim ibn Amr al-Qari

x: Others said: Rather, this is a valid exception, and the meaning of the statement is: Those who avoid major sins and indecencies, except for minor sins, unless he commits them and then repents.
Who said that?

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Abu Asim told us: Zakariya ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities

, except minor sins. He said: It is a man who commits an immoral act and then repents. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive many, and which servant of yours is there who does not forgive?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said:
m: In this verse, except for the touch, he said: the one who touches the sin and then abandons it. And the poet said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive a lot, and which servant of yours is there without pain?

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie’ told me: Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah,
m: who I think traced it back to the Prophet:
h
Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities

, except minor sins. He said: The minor sin is adultery, then he repents and does not return to it, and the minor sin is theft, then he repents and does not return to it, and the minor sin is drinking alcohol, then he repents and does not return to it. He said: That is the minor sin.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities
, except minor sins, he said, The minor sins are adultery, theft, or drinking alcohol, then one does not do it again.

c: Yaqoub told me: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities
, except minor sins, he said, The minor sins are adultery, theft, or drinking alcohol, then one does not do it again.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities

, except minor sins, he said: The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: This man commits a minor sin, such as fornication or drinking alcohol, but he conceals it and then repents from it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Except for a touch. He touches it at once. I said: Adultery. He said: Adultery then he repents.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us: Muammar said:
m: Al-Hasan used to say about the limmah: A man may limmah to an immoral act and then repent.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh, who said:
m: Adultery, then he repents. He said: It was narrated to us by Mihran on the authority of Abu Jaafar on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Al-Hasan:
h
Except for a small amount
. He said: That the incident occurs and then it stops.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Al-Lammam means the one who touches something once.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said: Yahya ibn Ayoub told me on the authority of Al-Muthanna ibn Al-Sabah on the authority of Amr ibn Shuaib that Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-As said:
m: The minor sin is less than polytheism.
b.via: that Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-As

x: God Almighty says: Have you seen, O Muhammad, the one who turned away from faith in God and turned away from Him and His religion and gave his companion a little of his wealth and then withheld from him and did not give him anything, so he was miserly with him? It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira because some of the polytheists rebuked him. He had followed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his religion, so the one who rebuked him guaranteed that if he gave him some of his money and returned to his polytheism, he would bear the punishment of the Hereafter on his behalf. So he did so, and he gave the one who rebuked him for that some of what he had guaranteed him, then he was stingy with him and prevented him from the full amount he had guaranteed him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and he was steadfast, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira said, He gave a little, then he was steadfast.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God, Have you seen him who turns away? until the statement, so he sees? He said: This is a man who had become Muslim and was met by someone who was taunting him. He said: You have abandoned the religion of the elders and led them astray and claimed that they are in the Fire. It was incumbent upon you to support them, but what will be the case with your fathers? He said: I feared the punishment of God. He said: Give me something and I will bear every punishment that was upon you. So he gave him something. He said: Give me more. So he struggled until he gave him something and wrote him a letter and bore witness for him. This is the statement of God, Have you seen him who turns away and is given little and is hard-pressed? “Does he have knowledge of the unseen so he sees?” This verse was revealed concerning him. And Binjo, whom we mentioned in the meaning of his saying and he emphasized, said the people of interpretation.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan al-Shaibani, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He gave a little and then stopped. He said: He gave a little and then stopped.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Have you seen he who turns away and gives little and is stingy
? He says: He gives little and then stops.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: and He gave a little and he was given nothing he said: It was cut off so he was not given anything. Haven’t you seen the well called Akkad?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And his stipend was cut off.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus and Qatadah,
m: regarding his statement, and he gave a little, he said: He gave a little, then stopped that. Have you seen him who turned away? He said: Ibn Thaur told us, he said:

c: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: And he was stingy means he was stingy and his stinginess was cut off.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, and he was afflicted, meaning his stipend was cut off.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about his statement and akadda and Akada Asira and the Arabs say: So-and-so dug and akadda, and that is when he reached the kaddaa, which is when a man digs in the plain and then faces a mountain and he digs it. It is said that he has akadda, and his nails and fingers became thick and deficient, if they became thick and his fingers became tired and did not work at all, and the girl’s income is little, with a hamzah.

x: Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language say that his statement akadda is derived from kaddaa which is that he digs until he despairs of water, so it is said at that time we have reached her kaddaa.
God Almighty says: And He gave little and was straitened.
And His statement:
h
Does he have knowledge of the unseen

, so that he sees? God Almighty says: Does this person, to whom his companion promised that he would bear God’s punishment on his behalf in the Hereafter, have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees the truth of his words and his fulfillment of what he promised him?
And His statement:
h
Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses
? God Almighty says: Or has this person not been informed that he will bear the punishment of God in the Hereafter because of what is in the scriptures of Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him?
And his saying:
h
And Abraham who fulfilled
means:
h
And Abraham who fulfilled
what he was sent to. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of who fulfilled.
Some of them said that it was his fulfillment of what his Lord had entrusted him with, which was to convey His messages, which is: No soul shall bear the burden of another.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And Abraham who fulfilled

. He said: Before Abraham, they used to take guardians to guardians until Abraham came and he reached: No soul shall bear the burden of another. No one shall be held accountable for the sin of another.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And Abraham who fulfilled

he said: And fulfilled the obedience of God and conveyed the messages of his Lord to His creation. And Ikrimah used to say: And in these ten verses it says: No soul shall bear the burden of another… until he reached: And upon Him is the next life.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement:
h
And Abraham who fulfilled in obeying God and His messages to His creation
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me: Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And Abraham who fulfilled
, he said: He conveyed what he was commanded to do.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan and Ibrahim
m: who fulfilled, saying: He conveyed.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And Abraham who fulfilled
, he said: He fulfilled and conveyed the messages of his Lord. He conveyed what he was sent with, just as a man conveys what he was sent with.

x: Others said: Rather, he fulfilled what he saw in the dream of slaughtering his son. They said that his statement, No soul shall bear the burden of another is from the deferred meaning of the forward. They said: The meaning of the statement is, Or was he not informed of what is in the scrolls of Moses, ‘No soul shall bear the burden of another’, and what is in the scrolls of Abraham, who fulfilled.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My paternal uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: regarding his statement,
h
Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses * and Abraham who fulfilled

? He says: Abraham is the one who completed the obedience in what he did with his son when he saw the vision, and what is in the scriptures of Moses is, No soul shall bear the burden of another, to the end of the verse.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Abu Sakhr on the authority of Al-Qurazi,
m: and he was asked about this verse:
h
And Abraham who fulfilled
. He said: He fulfilled his promise by sacrificing his son.
b.via: Abu Sakhr on the authority of Al-Qurazi

x: Others said that this means that he fulfilled all the laws of Islam to his Lord.
Who said that?

c: Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Shabwa told us: Ali bin Al-Hassan told us: Kharijah bin Musaab told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of And Abraham,
m: who fulfilled Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Islam is thirty arrows, and no one was afflicted with this religion and established it except Abraham. God said,
h
And Abraham who fulfilled
, so God wrote for him a release from the Fire.

c: Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And Abraham who fulfilled
what was imposed upon him.

x: Others said that he fulfilled what was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith that...

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Rashdin bin Saad told us: Ziyad bin Faid told us, on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Shall I not tell you why God called Abraham His faithful friend? Because he used to say every morning and evening: ‘Glory be to God when you go to bed at night and when you wake up in the morning,’ until he finished the verse.”

x: Others said: Rather, he fulfilled his Lord’s daily work.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Al-Hasan bin Atiyah told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:
h
And Abraham who fulfilled

. He said: Do you know what he fulfilled? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: And in the work of his day, four rakʿahs during the day. The most correct of the statements on this matter is the statement of those who said: And in the laws of Islam and all that he commanded of obedience, because God Almighty mentioned that he fulfilled it, so the statement about his fulfilling it included all obedience and did not specify some over others.

x: If someone were to say that he limited that to his statement, And in * that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, then that is something that God, the Most High, has informed us is in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham, not something that he limited the report to, that he fulfilled. As for the fulfillment, then it is general. Even if the two reports that we mentioned, or one of them, were authentic from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, we would not have attributed it to anyone else, but there is a problem with their chain of transmission, for which verification is necessary.
And his saying:
h
No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another

, then from his saying no bearer of burdens according to the interpretation we have interpreted it is in the position of a genitive in response to what is in his saying Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses? He means by his saying
h
no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another

other than her, rather every sinner, then her sin is upon her. We have explained the interpretation of this based on the differences among scholars in what has passed before. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told us: Abu Malik Al-Janbi told us: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ghifari
m: regarding his statement,
h
No soul shall bear the burden of another
, and that man shall have nothing but what he strives for, to His statement, of the first vows, he said, This is in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. Rather, what he meant by his saying,
h
No soul shall bear the burden of another

, is what he guaranteed to Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira that he would bear the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection. He says: Did not the one who said this statement and the one who guaranteed this guarantee inform us of what is written in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham that no sinner shall bear the sin of another and that man shall have nothing but what he strives for, and God Almighty says: Or did He not inform us that no worker will be rewarded except for his work, whether it be good or evil?

c: As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And that man can have nothing but what he strives for
, and he recited, Indeed, your striving is diverse (al-Layl 92:4), he said: Your deeds.

c: It was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he said that this verse was abrogated.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And that man can have nothing but what he strives for

. He said: Then God revealed after this, And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring. (al-Tur 52:21) So the children will enter Paradise through the righteousness of their fathers.

x: His Most High saying: And that his effort will be seen. God Almighty says: And that the work of every worker will be seen on the Day of Resurrection from the time of Resurrection with the recompense for which he will be rewarded, whether good or evil. He will not be held accountable for the punishment of a sin other than that of his worker, nor will any worker other than him be rewarded for his good work. Rather, what is meant by that is the one who turned away from his Islam with his friend’s guarantee that he will bear the punishment on his behalf, that his guarantee will not benefit him or avail him at all on the Day of Resurrection, because every worker will be held accountable for his knowledge.
And His statement:
h
Then He will reward him with the fullest reward

. God Almighty says: Then he will be rewarded for his effort with that fullest reward. God Almighty only said the fullest because He fulfilled what He promised His creation for it in terms of reward. The ha in His statement,
h
Then He will reward him is from the mention of the effort
, and it returned to that.
And His statement:
h
And to your Lord is the final destination

. God Almighty says: To His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to your Lord, O Muhammad, is the final destination and return of all His creation. He is the One who will reward all of them for their deeds, the righteous and the wicked, the good and the evil.
And His statement:
h
And that it is He who makes laugh and cry God Almighty says

: And that your Lord is He who makes laugh the people of Paradise in Paradise by entering it and makes cry the people of Hell in Hell by entering it and makes laugh whomever He wants from the people of this world and makes cry whomever He wants to make cry from them.

God Almighty says that He is the One who caused death among His creation, and He gives life to those among them who live. What He meant by His saying gives life is the breathing of the soul into the dead sperm, making it alive by placing the soul in it.
And His statement,
h
And that He created the two mates

, the male and the female, from a sperm-drop when it is emitted, God Almighty says: And that He innovated the creation of the two mates, the male and the female, and made them two mates, because the male is the mate of the female and the female has a mate, so they are two mates, each of them being a mate for the other.
And His saying, from a sperm-drop when it is emitted, and from is a connection to creation. God Almighty says: He created that from a sperm-drop when the man and woman ejaculated.

And His statement, And that upon Him is the other creation, the Almighty says: And that your Lord, O Muhammad, will create these two pairs after their death and their trial in their graves with the other creation, and that is to bring them back to life as a new creation as they were before their death.
God Almighty says: And your Lord is richer than any of His creation in wealth and has provided him with wealth and made for him the means of obtaining wealth.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this verse.
Some of them said what we said about it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: regarding his statement, enriched and satisfied, he said: enriched with money and satisfied with property.

x: Others said about me, when he said, I am rich, that is, I serve.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, And that He is the One who enriches and provides, he said: Enriches is a master and provides: He serves.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Abu Raja’ on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement, enriched and satisfied, he said: and served.
b.via: Abu Raja’ on the authority of Al-Hasan

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, enriched and satisfied, he said: enriched and served.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, enriched and satisfied, he said: gave, satisfied, and served.

x: Others said that he meant that he was richer than money and satisfied.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And that He is the Most Rich and the Most Satisfied
, he said: For He is the Most Rich and the Most Satisfied.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And that He is the Most Enriching and the Most Satisfying. He said: The one who enriches and is satisfied means being pleased.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, enriched, he said: made him a master, and satisfied, he said: satisfied.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And that He is the One who enriches and satisfies him, meaning: He gave him and satisfied him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: like the hadith of Ibn Bashar, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Sufyan.

x: Others said that he meant that he enriched himself and made his creation poorer to him.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us on the authority of his father:
m: And that He is the richest and most content. He said: A Hadrami claimed that it was mentioned to him that He is the richest of himself and the poorest of creation to Him.

x: Others said that he meant that he enriched whomever he wanted of his creation and impoverished whomever he wanted.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, And that He is the Most Enriched and the Most Satisfied, he said: He enriched and increased, and He satisfied and decreased. And he recited, He expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him
r
(Saba’: 36)

x: And His statement,
h
And that He is the Lord of Sirius
, God Almighty says: And that your Lord, O Muhammad, is the
h
Lord of Sirius

. He means by Sirius: the star called by this name, which is a star that some of the people of ignorance used to worship instead of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And that He is the Lord of Sirius
, he said, It is the star called Sirius.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Ali bin Sahl told me: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And that He is the Lord of Sirius
, he said: The planet behind Gemini, they used to worship it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And that He is the Lord of Sirius
. He said: It was worshipped in the pre-Islamic era.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Lord of Sirius
, he said: Marzam is the star of Gemini.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And that He is the Lord of Sirius
, there was a tribe of Arabs who worshipped Sirius, this star that you saw. Bishr said: He means the star that follows Gemini.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Lord of Sirius
, that they used to worship this star called Sirius in the pre-Islamic era.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And that He is the Lord of Sirius

, it was worshipped in the pre-Islamic period. So he said: Do you worship this and abandon its Lord? Worship its Lord. He said: Sirius is the blazing star that follows Gemini, and it is called Al-Mirzam.

x: And His statement, And that He destroyed the former ‘Aad, means that the former ‘Aad were ‘Aad, son of Iram, son of Aws, son of Sam, son of Noah, and they are the ones whom God destroyed with a furious, violent wind, and He meant them with His statement, Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ‘Aad, Iram? (al-Fajr 89:6-7). The reciters differed in their recitation of this, so the majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the reciters of Basra recited it, leaving the hamza and jazm of the noon until the lam in al-ala became like a heavy lam. The Arabs do that in such a case.

c: It was reported from them
m: that they heard it from them. Qum because ‘anna means Qum now. They jazm the meem when the lam with the alif in al-an was moved. Likewise, you say Sam Ithnayn meaning Sam al-Ithnayn. As for the majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the Meccans, they recited it by making the noon pronounced and kasra and jazm of the first letter, with differences in that from al-A’mash. His companions narrated from him, except for al-Qasim bin Ma’n, that he agreed with the people of his country in that. As for al-Qasim bin Ma’n, it was reported from al-A’mash that he agreed with the recitation of the Medinans in that. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what we mentioned from the Kufians, because that is the eloquent speech of the Arabs, and the reading of those who are people of natural disposition is based on clarity and emphasis, and assimilation in such a letter and leaving clarity is only permitted for those who have that in their nature and disposition from the people of the desert. As for those who are born, their rule is that they should seek out the most eloquent, sweetest, and most reliable readings, even if the other ones are permissible and not rejected. And it was said that Ad bin Iram was the first Ad because the sons of Luqaym bin Hazal bin Ubail bin Dhadd bin Ad the elder were, at the time when God sent His punishment upon Ad the elder, living in Mecca with their brothers from the Amalekites, the sons of Amalek bin Lawdh bin Sam bin Noah, and they were not with their people from Ad in their land, so the punishment that befell their people did not afflict them, and they are the Ad of the Hereafter, and then they perished after that. The destruction of the people of Ad in the Hereafter was due to the aggression of some of them against others, so they were killed in the killing.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: as we mentioned, that the greater ‘Ad, whose descendants God destroyed with the wind, was called the first ‘Ad because they were destroyed before the last ‘Ad. Ibn Zayd used to say: The first ‘Ad was called that because they were the first of the nations to be destroyed.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, He destroyed the first ‘Aad, that it is said: They are among the first nations.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this, so the majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the reciters of Basra recited it, leaving the hamza and jazm of the noon until the lam in al-ala became like a heavy lam.
As for the majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the Meccans, they recited it by making the noon pronounced and kasra and jazm of the first letter, with differences in that from al-A’mash.
As for al-Qasim bin Ma’n, it was reported from al-A’mash that he agreed with the recitation of the Medinans in that.

The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what we mentioned from the Kufians, because that is the eloquent speech of the Arabs, and the reading of those who are people of natural disposition is based on clarity and emphasis, and assimilation in such a letter and leaving clarity is only permitted for those who have that in their nature and disposition from the people of the desert.

x: And His statement, And Thamud - what did He leave behind? God Almighty says: God did not leave Thamud behind, leaving them in their transgression and rebellion against their Lord, but He punished them for their disbelief and insolence, so He destroyed them. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Basra and some of the Kufians read it as and Thamud, so what did He leave in accordance with the procedure, following the Qur’an, since the alif was fixed in it.

Some of the majority of the Kufians read it without the procedure, and it was mentioned that it is in the Qur’an of Abdullah without the alif. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites is correct, because they are both correct in terms of grammar and meaning. We have explained the story of Thamud and the reason for their destruction previously, so there is no need to repeat it.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of this.
The majority of the reciters of Basra and some of the Kufians read it as and Thamud, so what did He leave in accordance with the procedure, following the Qur’an, since the alif was fixed in it.
Some of the majority of the Kufians read it without the procedure, and it was mentioned that it is in the Qur’an of Abdullah without the alif.

x: God Almighty says: And that He destroyed the people of Noah before them, Aad and Thamud. Indeed, they were more unjust to themselves, more disbelieving in their Lord, and more rebellious and disobedient to God than those nations whom He destroyed after them. And their rebellion was what God described them with, and they were thus more rebellious than other nations.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
And the people of Noah before them

. Indeed, they were more unjust and more rebellious.” There was no tribe of people more unjust and more rebellious than the people of Noah. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them for a thousand years minus fifty years. Whenever a generation perished and a generation arose, the Prophet of God called them until he mentioned to us that a man would take his son by the hand and walk with him, saying, O my son, my father walked with me to this point, and I am like you, and I will be like you on that day, following one another in misguidance and denial of the command of God.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, they were more unjust and more rebellious, he said, The Prophet of God called them for a thousand years minus fifty years.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

x: And His statement,
h
And the overturned city

, I have cast it down. God Almighty says: And the city that was overturned, its top being its bottom, and it is the city of Sodom, the people of Lot, God cast it down, so He commanded Gabriel, peace and blessings be upon him, to lift it from the seventh earth with his wing, then He cast it down upside down. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And the one that was overturned, He inclined. He said: Gabriel inclined it. He said: He raised it to the sky and then made it fall.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Ibn Isa Yahya Ibn Rafi’:
m: h
And the overturned city
I am falling into. He said: The village of Lot when I fall into it.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the overturned city
I incline towards, he said: The village of Lot.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And the overturned ones I desire, he said: They are the people of Lot.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the overturned city
, I cast down, that the village of Lot was brought down from the sky, then that rock followed it, uprooted from the earth, then he cast it down into the sky, then it was turned upside down.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And the overturned ones I incline towards, he said, The deniers, may God destroy them.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

x: And His statement, And that which covered it covered it, God Almighty says: So God covered the overturned city with that which covered it, and He rained down upon it of baked clay. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And what covered it covered it covered it with layered rocks.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: What covered her covered her means: stones.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, And that which covered them covered them, he said: The stones that He threw at them from the sky.

x: He says,
h
Then which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute

? God Almighty says: Then which of the favors of your Lord, O son of Adam, which He has bestowed upon you do you doubt, suspect, and argue? The favors are the plural of to, and there are three forms for the singular form: to, for example, on, and to, for example, on, and to, for example, ala. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute
? He said: Then which of the favors of God do you dispute, O son of Adam?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Then which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute
? He said: Which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute?
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

x: And his saying,
h
This is a warner among the first warners
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His saying, may His praise be exalted, to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
This is a warner among the first warners
, and His description of him as being among the first warners and the last of them.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is that he is a warner to his people, and the warners who came before him were warners to their people, just as one says: This is one of the children of Adam and one of the people.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
This is a warner among the first warners
, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was warned just as the messengers before him were warned.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
This is a warner among the first warners
, that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent with what the messengers before him were sent with.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar:
m: This is a warner from the first warners. He said: He is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said that the meaning of this is different from all of this and they said: Its meaning is this that I warned you of, O people, from the events that I mentioned to you that I brought about with the nations before you from the warnings that I warned the nations before you in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Malik:
m: This is a warning from the first warnings. He said: Among the things with which they warned their people in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. What I mentioned about Abu Malik is more similar to the interpretation of the verse, and that is that God Almighty mentioned it in the context of the verses that He informed us about, which are in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses, and a warner from the first warners that came to the nations before you, just as they came to you. So his saying, This is to be a reference to what preceded it in speech, is more appropriate and similar to something else.

x: And his saying,
h
The approaching event has drawn near
, means:
h
The approaching event has drawn near

. What he means is that the Resurrection has drawn near to you, O people. It is said from this that the departure of so-and-so has drawn near, as Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan said: The departure time has come, but our passengers have not yet left our saddlebags, as if they had As Kaab bin Zuhair said: Youth has passed and gray hair has come, and I see no successor to the departing youth. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
The approaching hour has drawn near
. One of the names of the Day of Resurrection is the greatness of God and His warning to His servants.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
The approaching hour has drawn near
, he said, The Hour has drawn near.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
The approaching hour has drawn near
, that it is the Hour, for which there is none to avert but God.

x: And His statement,
h
There is none to avert it besides God

. God the Almighty says: The approaching Hour, which is the Hour that has drawn near, has none to avert it besides God. He says, it will not be revealed and come to pass except by God establishing it and revealing it without anyone else from His creation, because no close angel or sent prophet has seen it. It was said, Kashfah, but it was made feminine, and it means uncovering, as was said, Do you see for them any remainder? (al-Haqqah 69:8), meaning do you see for them any remainder? And as was said, The outcome, and what it has of a deterrent; and as was said, There is no denier of its occurrence (al-Waqi’ah 56:2), meaning denial; And it will not cease to uncover treachery among them. (al-Ma’idah 5:13), meaning treachery.

God Almighty says to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:“O people, is it this Qur’an that you are amazed at, that it was sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that you laugh at it in mockery of it and do not cry because of what it contains of threats to those who disobey God, while you are among those who disobey Him?”
h
And you are heedless

means leave us alone with your amusement. It is said from it samd “samud” meaning, to be heedless. And in a similar manner to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation said, although their expressions differed regarding it.
Some of them said, Heedless, some of them said, Enriched, and some of them said, Distracted.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, samidun, he said: It is singing. When they heard the Qur’an, they would sing and play, and it is the language of the people of Yemen. The Yemeni said: Asmad.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Samidon, meaning: heedless.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you are heedless
, meaning: distracted.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: She is a Yemeni woman, Asmad, singing for us.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: It is singing, and it is Yemeni. They say, Sing for us, and we will sing for you. He said: Ubaidullah Al-Ashja’i narrated to us on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Hakim bin Al-Daylam on the authority of Al-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And you are standing tall. He said: They would pass by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing tall. Have you not seen the stallion among the camels, standing tall and proud?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And you are heedless
, he said: Heedless.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And you are steadfast

. He said: They would pass by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, angry and gloating. Ikrimah said: It is singing in the Himyarite dialect. He said: Al-Ashja’i and Waki’ narrated to us on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid who said: It is the bartama.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you are steadfast
, he said: The Bartama.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Abu Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And you are steadfast
, he said: The Bartama.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The Samidun are the singers in the Himyarite dialect.

c: Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Ikrimah used to say: The Samidun sing in the Himyarite dialect, and Ibn Abbas is not in it.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Samidun meaning heedless.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, Samidun, he said: Heedless.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Regarding His statement, and you are idling, idling means amusement and play.

c: Humaid bin Masada told us: Yazid bin Zari’ told us: Sufyan bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Fitr, on the authority of Abu Khalid al-Walabi, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: He saw them standing, waiting for the Imam, so he said: What is wrong with you, why are you standing?

c: Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Imran bin Zaida bin Nasheet, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Khalid, who said:
m: Ali, may God be pleased with him, came out to us while we were standing and said: Why do I see you standing? He said: Abu Asim told us:

c: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Fitr, on the authority of Zaida,
m: on the Do you then wonder at this statement? authority of Abu Khalid, something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement, And you are staying up, he said, standing at night before the imam comes.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Imran al-Khayyat, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding the people waiting for the prayer while standing. He said: It was said that was the Samud.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Layth and Al-Azrami, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And you are steadfast
. He said: The burtum.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And you are steadfast
. He said: Singing in Yemeni means sing for us.

c: Yunus told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And you are heedless
. He said, Heedless means heedless.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: They used to hate to stand when the muezzin called for prayer and the imam was not with them, and they used to hate to wait for him to stand, and it was said: That is the samud or from the samud.

x: God Almighty says: And you laugh and do not cry.
And God Almighty said, And you are steadfast.
And His statement,
h
So prostrate to God and worship Him

, God Almighty says: So prostrate to God, O people, in your prayers, without any other gods or rivals besides Him, and worship Him alone, for worship should not be for anyone but Him, so devote your worship and prostration to Him and do not make any partner for Him in your worship of Him.
Commentary on Sūrat The Star (al-Najm). In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

notes.en: Al-Mirzamān are two stars. Together with al-Shiʿrayān they form the stars called al-Dhirāʿ: the forearm lies in one of the two Mirzams, and the pattern of al-Jawzāʾ forms the other. Their arrangement consists of stars with the two Mirzams, which are the Mirzams of al-Shiʿrayān; the two Shiʿrā stars, with the two forearms beside them, form the rest of the configuration. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root r-z-m.

notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 629. وأخرجه أبو الشيخ في العظمة (371) من طريق أبي عاصم به، وأخرجه (372) من طريق ابن أبي نجيح به. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 131 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 131 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر، وفي المخطوطة المحمودية ص 398 عزاه إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد.

notes.en: The original manuscript reads: “in the Mother of the Book.” See al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ (8/170).
notes.ar: في الأصل: "في أم الكتاب". وينظر البحر المحيط 8/ 170.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr (6/131) to the author, with the wording: “Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, warned of what earlier messengers warned.” The Maḥmūdiyyah manuscript, p. 398, reads: “This is in the scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā.”
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 131 إلى المصنف، بلفظ: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أنذر ما أنذر الأولون. وفي المخطوطة المحمودية ص 398 بلفظ: هذا في صحف إبراهيم وموسى.

notes.en: Ṣād, Mīm, T1, T2, and T3: “that which you mentioned.”
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "الذي ذكرت".

notes.ar: ديوانه ص 30، وفيه: "أفِد" مكان "أزف". وهما روايتان بمعنًى.

notes.ar: في ص: "لم".

notes.ar: شرح ديوانه ص 70.

notes.ar:
عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 131 إلى المصنف، دون قوله: "عظمه 
…. إلخ".

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 629; al-Firyābī transmitted it through him—as cited in Taghlīq al-taʿlīq (4/322). Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr (6/131) to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 629، ومن طريقه الفريابي - كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 322 - وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 131 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: Ṣād, Mīm, and T1 read “and it was said, ‘kāshifah,’” with the feminine form; T2 and T3 read “and it was said: ‘kāshifah,’” affirming it.
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1: "وقيل كاشفة. فأنثت"، وفي ت 2، ت 3: "وقيل: كاشفة. فأثبت".

notes.en: Omitted in T2 and T3. The original manuscript reads: “meaning, do you see anyone who remains for them?” See the commentary on this verse at its proper place below.
notes.ar: سقط من: ت 2، ت 3. وفي الأصل: "بمعنى هل ترى لهم مَنْ بقى"، وينظر ما سيأتي في تفسير هذه الآية في موضعه من التفسير.

notes.ar: في م: "قيل".

notes.en: The original manuscript reads “murtamūn”; Ṣād, T1, T2, and T3 read “mutaraṭṭimūn.” Al-birṭimah is a scowl with puffed cheeks and anger; it also means swelling from rage. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root b-r-ṭ-m.
notes.ar: في الأصل: "مرطمون"، وفي ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "مترطمون". والبرطمة عبوس في انتفاخ وغيظ. والبرطمة: الانتفاخ من الغضب. اللسان (برطم).
